newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shamed by Albania flagship fiasco.
newsitem.headline: Italy shamed by Albania flagship fiasco.

text.p: Image-conscious Italy reeled with embarrassment on Wednesday after its navy flagship got stuck on a sandbank in Albania one week into a major security mission.
In a land where "bella figura" -- or looking good -- is everything, the mishap at the start of the first international military operation to be led by Italy was greeted with derision.
"Ugly Italian spectacle in Vlore," ran the banner headline in rightist daily Il Giornale. "First Albanian 'brutta figura'".
Il Messaggero made light of the spectacle of the huge cruiser, the Vittorio Veneto, marooned off the southern port of Vlore for a day until tugs finally freed it on Wednesday.
"First success of the humanitarian mission in Albania," quipped a front-page cartoon showing Albanians jeering in the port as the ship's officers looked on, horrified.
"Poor things, at least we've given them something to laugh about," it said.
Italian navy officials said they had begun an internal investigation into the incident.

Italy is leading an eight-nation force dubbed Operation Alba to protect humanitarian aid deliveries to the Balkan state following weeks of chaos since the collapse of dubious savings schemes. Rebels are still in control of much of the south.

The mission started impressively as the first contingents of 6,000 heavily-armed troops landed and began deploying up and down the country. But they have had little to do so far, making the stranded ship's predicament even more poignant.
General Luciano Forlani, commander of the multinational force, was sanguine.
"These things happen," he said. "The Vittorio Veneto was at anchor, there was a strong wind. What more is there to say?"
Newspapers, which all splashed the story over several pages, pointed out that Italy should have known better.
Fascist troops of dictator Benito Mussolini came to grief on sandbanks in the same notoriously shallow harbour when they invaded Albania in 1939.
Another Italian ship, the Regina Margherita, was wrecked after running aground and hitting a mine in Vlore during World War One. Some 650 crew died.
La Repubblica said the Vittorio Veneto was left like a "beached whale" after the accident on Tuesday morning.
Speculation flew on Wednesday about the cause of the accident, which happened after an Italian navy ship had spent hours combing Vlore port for mines.
Admiral Mario Porta, an ex-defence chief of staff and former commander of the flagship said the navy knew Vlore's problems.

"It is a terrible port...which hasn't been dredged for ages," he told La Stampa. "On top of that, like all Adriatic ports, it is subject to sand build-ups. But the navy knew that and sent a boat recently to check the depth."
One sailor said it was more than just bad luck.

"We sailors believe in fate and this mission to Albania was born under an unlucky star," he told La Repubblica, referring to the sinking last month of an Albanian boat after it collided with an Italian ship. More than 80 refugees died.
